title: Localization coordinates of the fixed ordered Cech mapping fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ generate $I$. For the fixed augmented fibre $(C_f,a_f)$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-ordered-cech-construction], there are $A$-linear coordinates $e_0:C_f^0\cong A$ and $e_q:C_f^{q+1}\cong\prod_{t:\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\hookrightarrow_o\operatorname{Fin}(r)}A_{\prod_i f_{t(i)}}$ for $q\geq0$, and face localization $A$-algebra maps $l_{q,t,j}$, such that $C_f^n=0$ for $n<0$, $e_0$ identifies $a_f^0$ with the identity, the first differential sends $x$ to its image in each localization, and $e_{q+1}(dx)_t=\sum_j(-1)^j l_{q,t,j}((e_qx)_{t\setminus j})$. Here each face deletes its indexed entry, as in [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. No derived comparison with Godement is asserted. The empty list, repeated or zero generators and the zero ring are included.

proof.text: Use the unaugmented ordered Cech section coordinates E_q and face algebra maps l. These identify the actual first restriction with the algebra map and its differential with the signed face sum.

The negative section terms vanish by extension by zero. The cone first projection is an isomorphism in degree -1, since its section summand vanishes, and its second projection is an isomorphism in nonnegative degrees, since the single-complex summand vanishes. Compose them with the inverse-shift term isomorphisms and evaluate on the one-object site. Both inverse identities follow from the mapping-cone id_X identity. Negative fibre terms vanish by mappingCone.isZero_X_iff.

The shifted differential is minus the cone differential. The d_snd_v formula gives minus the first restriction in fibre degree zero and minus the section differential in every positive degree. Multiply the q-th section coordinate by (-1)^(q+1), implemented by a power of the negation linear equivalence. Successive signs convert the first map to the algebra map and higher differentials to the signed face sum.

Expanding the inverse rotation in degree zero identifies its augmentation with the cone first projection. Its composition with the single-complex term isomorphism is exactly the chosen degree-zero coordinate, so the augmentation equation holds.

theorem ringComplexOrderedCech_coordinates (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (I : Ideal A)
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    let C := ringComplexOrderedCech A I f
    let a := ringComplexOrderedCechAugmentation A I f
    ∃ (e₀ : (C.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A] A)
          (e : ∀ q : ℕ, (C.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A]
            ((t : Fin (q + 1) ↪o Fin r) → Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))))
          (l : ∀ (q : ℕ) (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r) (j : Fin (q + 2)),
            Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j i))) →ₐ[A]
              Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))),
          (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (C.X n)) ∧
          (∀ (x : (C.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin r),
            e 0 ((C.d 0 1).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
              algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))) (e₀ x)) ∧
          (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : (C.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
            (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r),
            e (q + 1) ((C.d ((q : ℤ) + 1) ((q : ℤ) + 2)).val.app
              (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
              ∑ j : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
                l q t j (e q x ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t))) ∧
          (∀ x : (C.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩),
            (a.f 0 ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0
              (SheafOfModules.unit.{u, u, u} ((sheafCompose ⊥
                (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
                  (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf.{u} A)))).hom).val.app
                    (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x = e₀ x)
